title: ci: assert every test vitest counted actually ran (#3825)
body:
Follow-up to #3830 / #3812.

## The failure mode

A vitest worker can die at the **process level** — a native module segfault, OOM, an abort inside a binding. There is no JS error to catch, so the cases that worker owned never run, and the summary reports only what survived:

```
Test Files  1 passed (40)
      Tests  21 passed (401)
```

That leads with **"passed"**. It is **380 tests short**.

#3812 hit exactly this shape (17 cases silently skipped, reported as `22 passed (23)`) and it was found by a human reading the log closely — which is not a control.

## Being precise about the risk

I want to be accurate rather than oversell this: **the run does exit non-zero, so the gate goes red.** This is not a false green.

The failure mode is **a red that reads like a pass**. Someone triaging sees "passed" and a plausible file count and concludes one file flaked — rather than that a fifth of the suite never executed. This PR turns that into a specific, quantified error naming the package and the shortfall. It also covers the genuinely dangerous variant, where a crash lands somewhere that does not propagate a non-zero exit at all.

## How

`scripts/check-test-completeness.mjs` reads a saved `turbo run test` log and asserts, per package, that the tallies (`passed | skipped | failed`) sum to the declared total. Reading the log rather than wrapping vitest means **no change to the 60+ per-package vitest configs**.

Wired into `ci.yml`'s Test Core (both PR and push steps) and both Dogfood shards, each as a separate `if: always()` step so it runs **when the suite failed** — that is when it earns its keep:

| Suite | Completeness | Means |
|---|---|---|
| red | green | real test failures |
| red | **red** | **a worker died; those cases never ran** |

## Two load-bearing details

**1. `set -o pipefail` is not optional.** The test steps now `tee`, and GitHub runs them with `bash -e`, which does **not** set pipefail — so `turbo … | tee` would report *tee's* exit status and a failing suite would go green. That is the same class of bug this guard exists to catch, so it must not be introduced by the catching. Verified both ways:

```
with    pipefail → step exits 7   ✅
without pipefail → step exits 0   ❌
```

Also confirmed the log still exists when the suite fails, so the `always()` guard can still read it.

**2. Zero summaries is a pass with an explicit note**, not a silent one — `turbo run test --affected` legitimately runs nothing when a PR touches no package. A vacuous pass that *looks* like a real one is the thing we are trying to eliminate, so it says so.

## Validation — real data, not fixtures

Run against the actual logs captured during #3830's Node 20 vs 22 comparison:

```
Node 22 log:  check-test-completeness: OK (68 package(s), 16678 test(s) declared
                                        and all 16678 accounted for).           exit 0

Node 20 log:  check-test-completeness: 2 summaries report fewer results than it counted
                • @objectstack/driver-sql -- Test Files: 1 of 40 accounted for, 39 missing
                • @objectstack/driver-sql -- Tests: 21 of 401 accounted for, 380 missing
                                                                                exit 1
```

That Node 20 log is a real worker segfault, not a constructed one.
